# Configuration reference

For operators. Every environment variable BudgetPilot reads, with its default and the values it accepts.
For what to change and why, read [Configuration](configuration.md) first.

<!-- Generated from src/lib/server/env/settings.ts. Do not edit by hand: change the registry, then run
     npx vitest run src/lib/server/env/settingsReference.spec.ts -u -->

Set these in the `.env` file next to your compose file, then restart. A whole number is written in the
digits 0 to 9 only: `0x10`, `1e3`, `12.0` and `1_000` are refused rather than read as a number you did
not write. An empty value is the same as leaving the variable out.

**Tier** says who needs it: « Set on every install » is the short list a new install must get right;
« Advanced » settings are safe to leave out.

## Instance

| Setting             | What it does                                                                                                                                     | Default                                          | Accepted values                                                 | Tier                 | Guide                                                           |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ORIGIN`            | The address people use to reach the app. Form submissions from any other origin are refused. Read by the SvelteKit Node adapter, not by the app. | http://localhost:<APP_PORT> under Docker Compose | The exact URL typed in the browser, without a trailing slash.   | Set on every install | [More](configuration.md#origin-has-to-be-exact)                 |
| `PUBLIC_INSTANCE`   | Whether session cookies are sent only over HTTPS. Set false only for a local network served over plain http.                                     | `true`                                           | `true`, `false`. Any other value is treated as true.            | Set on every install | [More](configuration.md#public_instance-and-the-session-cookie) |
| `REGISTRATION_MODE` | Who may create an account: only an administrator through an invitation, or anyone who reaches the sign-up page.                                  | `admin_only`                                     | `admin_only`, `open`. Any other value is treated as admin_only. | Common               | [More](configuration.md#who-can-create-an-account)              |
| `APP_PORT`          | The port Docker Compose publishes the app on, on the host. Read by Docker Compose, not by the app.                                               | 3000                                             | A TCP port number.                                              | Common               | [More](configuration.md)                                        |

## Secrets

| Setting                  | What it does                                                                                                                       | Default | Accepted values                                        | Tier                 | Guide                                                                |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`    | Encrypts every two-factor secret at rest. Changing it locks every user with two-factor out. **Secret:** never logged, never shown. | none    | 64 hexadecimal characters (`openssl rand -hex 32`).    | Set on every install | [More](configuration.md#the-three-secrets)                           |
| `RATE_LIMIT_HASH_SECRET` | Keys the hashes that stand in for addresses and account names in rate limits and logs. **Secret:** never logged, never shown.      | none    | 64 hexadecimal characters (`openssl rand -hex 32`).    | Set on every install | [More](configuration.md#the-three-secrets)                           |
| `BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN`        | Required to create the first administrator account. May be left blank once one exists. **Secret:** never logged, never shown.      | none    | Any string (`openssl rand -base64 32`).                | Set on every install | [More](configuration.md#the-three-secrets)                           |
| `BP_STRICT_SECRET_FILES` | When on, the app refuses to start if a file holding a secret can be read or replaced by another account. When off, it only warns.  | `off`   | `off`, `on`. Any other value stops the app at startup. | Advanced             | [More](configuration.md#refusing-to-start-on-an-exposed-secret-file) |

## Accounts and sessions

| Setting                         | What it does                                                                             | Default | Accepted values                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Tier     | Guide                                                         |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PASSWORD_HASH_COST`            | The bcrypt work factor for stored passwords. Raising it slows every sign-in, on purpose. | `12`    | 12 to 15 (bcrypt cost, each step doubles the time). Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: Each step doubles the time every sign-in takes: measured at 160 ms at 12 and 1.3 s at 15, so a higher value turns the sign-in form into a way to exhaust the server. | Common   | [More](configuration.md#passwords-and-sessions)               |
| `SESSION_TTL_DAYS`              | How long a sign-in lasts before the user must sign in again.                             | `30`    | 1 to 400 days. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: Chrome and Firefox keep a cookie for at most 400 days whatever the server asks, the limit the IETF cookie draft recommends, so a longer lifetime mostly keeps a copied cookie usable.                     | Common   | [More](configuration.md#passwords-and-sessions)               |
| `BP_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_HOURS` | How long a sign-in can go unused before it ends, within its lifetime.                    | `168`   | 1 to 720 hours. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: 720 hours is 30 days, the default sign-in lifetime, so a longer inactivity timeout would never end a session before SESSION_TTL_DAYS does at its default.                                                | Common   | [More](configuration.md#passwords-and-sessions)               |
| `INVITATION_TTL_HOURS`          | How long an invitation link stays valid.                                                 | `72`    | 1 to 720 hours. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: An invitation link is a credential anyone holding it can use. 720 hours is 30 days, the longest validity NIST SP 800-63B-4 gives a recovery code, for one sent by post abroad.                           | Common   | [More](configuration.md#passwords-and-sessions)               |
| `BP_RATE_LIMIT_IPV6_PREFIX`     | How many leading bits of an IPv6 address the sign-in limits count as one client.         | `56`    | 32 to 64 bits. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: An end site is given a /64 at the least, so above 64 one subscriber holds more than one counter, and choosing a new address resets the per-address limit.                                                 | Advanced | [More](configuration.md#how-attempts-are-counted-per-address) |

## Database

| Setting             | What it does                                                                                                                                                                       | Default                                | Accepted values                                                                                   | Tier                 | Guide                             |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `DATABASE_PROVIDER` | Which database engine to use.                                                                                                                                                      | `sqlite`                               | `sqlite`, `postgresql`, `postgres`, `mysql`, `mariadb`. Any other value stops the app at startup. | Set on every install | [More](configuration.md#database) |
| `DATABASE_URL`      | Where the database is. With a server engine it carries the password. **Secret:** never logged, never shown.                                                                        | file:/data/budgetpilot.db in the image | A connection string whose scheme matches DATABASE_PROVIDER.                                       | Set on every install | [More](configuration.md#database) |
| `DATABASE_PASSWORD` | Password of the database server the PostgreSQL and MySQL Compose overlays start. SQLite ignores it. **Secret:** never logged, never shown. Read by Docker Compose, not by the app. | none                                   | 64 hexadecimal characters (`openssl rand -hex 32`).                                               | Common               | [More](database-providers.md)     |

## Reverse proxy

| Setting           | What it does                                                                                                                      | Default | Accepted values                              | Tier     | Guide                    |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------ |
| `TRUSTED_PROXIES` | The proxies whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed. Unset, the connecting address is the client.                                | none    | Comma-separated IP addresses or CIDR ranges. | Common   | [More](reverse-proxy.md) |
| `ADDRESS_HEADER`  | Read by the Node adapter, which would trust the header from anyone. The app refuses to start when it is set; use TRUSTED_PROXIES. | none    | Must stay unset.                             | Advanced | [More](reverse-proxy.md) |
| `XFF_DEPTH`       | Read by the Node adapter together with ADDRESS_HEADER. The app refuses to start when it is set; use TRUSTED_PROXIES.              | none    | Must stay unset.                             | Advanced | [More](reverse-proxy.md) |

## Uploads and imports

| Setting                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                      | Default                       | Accepted values                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Tier     | Guide                                                                  |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT`                 | The largest request body accepted, sized for a backup restore. It does not change the statement import limit. Read by the SvelteKit Node adapter, not by the app. | 21000000 in the Compose files | A number of bytes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Advanced | [More](configuration.md#upload-size)                                   |
| `IMPORT_XLSX_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_MB` | How much an uploaded .xlsx file may expand to when unpacked.                                                                                                      | `8`                           | 1 to 32 megabytes. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: A workbook expanding to 32 MB takes about a second to parse and holds the server while it does (#254).                   | Advanced | [More](configuration.md#upload-size)                                   |
| `BACKUP_MAX_JSON_NODES`           | How many separate values a restored backup may contain.                                                                                                           | `2000000`                     | 1 to 4,000,000 values. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: A backup carrying 4,000,000 values already costs about 214 MB of memory to parse, before any validation runs (#276). | Advanced | [More](configuration.md#backup-size)                                   |
| `CSV_MAX_COLUMNS`                 | How many columns an imported statement may have.                                                                                                                  | `512`                         | 1 to 4,096 columns. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: The column count multiplies the cost of every row the parser reads, and no bank export comes near it.                   | Advanced | [More](configuration.md#how-many-columns-a-statement-may-have)         |
| `COLUMN_MAPPINGS_PER_USER`        | How many saved column mappings one account may keep.                                                                                                              | `50`                          | 1 to 500 mappings. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: Every saved mapping is compared against each upload, so the count bounds the work one upload causes.                     | Advanced | [More](configuration.md#how-many-column-mappings-one-account-may-keep) |
| `IMPORT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS`  | How many statement uploads one account may make in 15 minutes.                                                                                                    | `60`                          | 1 to 240 uploads per 15 minutes. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: Above 240 the limit no longer stops one account from keeping the parser busy for everyone.                 | Advanced | [More](configuration.md#how-many-uploads-one-account-may-make)         |

## Bank sync

| Setting                              | What it does                                                                                          | Default                       | Accepted values                                                                                                                                                             | Tier     | Guide                |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------- |
| `BANK_SYNC_ENABLED`                  | Turns on bank synchronisation through Enable Banking.                                                 | `false`                       | `false`, `true`. Any other value is treated as false.                                                                                                                       | Common   | [More](bank-sync.md) |
| `BANK_SYNC_ALLOWED_HOSTS`            | The only hosts bank synchronisation may call, always over https.                                      | api.enablebanking.com         | Comma-separated host names; a value replaces the default.                                                                                                                   | Advanced | [More](bank-sync.md) |
| `BANK_SYNC_REDIRECT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | The origins a bank consent may return to. Unset, no bank connection can start.                        | none                          | Comma-separated origins, exactly as registered with Enable Banking.                                                                                                         | Common   | [More](bank-sync.md) |
| `BANK_SYNC_FIRST_LOOKBACK_DAYS`      | How far back a first synchronisation asks the bank for transactions.                                  | `90`                          | 1 to 3,650 days. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: Ten years is beyond what any bank serves through PSD2. | Advanced | [More](bank-sync.md) |
| `ENABLE_BANKING_APP_ID`              | Identifies this instance to Enable Banking.                                                           | none                          | The application id from the Enable Banking Control Panel.                                                                                                                   | Common   | [More](bank-sync.md) |
| `ENABLE_BANKING_PRIVATE_KEY`         | The private key that signs requests to Enable Banking, inline. **Secret:** never logged, never shown. | none                          | A PEM private key, newlines written as \\n; set this or the _PATH form, never both.                                                                                         | Common   | [More](bank-sync.md) |
| `ENABLE_BANKING_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH`    | The private key that signs requests to Enable Banking, as a file.                                     | none                          | A path to a PEM file, readable by the app; set this or the inline form, never both.                                                                                         | Common   | [More](bank-sync.md) |
| `ENABLE_BANKING_BASE_URL`            | The Enable Banking API address.                                                                       | https://api.enablebanking.com | An https URL whose host is in BANK_SYNC_ALLOWED_HOSTS.                                                                                                                      | Advanced | [More](bank-sync.md) |

## AI insights

| Setting                    | What it does                                                                        | Default                   | Accepted values                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Tier     | Guide                         |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `LLM_ENABLED`              | Turns on the optional insights written by a local model.                            | `false`                   | `false`, `true`. Any other value is treated as false.                                                                                                                                                                                               | Common   | [More](ai-insights.md)        |
| `LLM_PROVIDER`             | Which model server to call. Only Ollama exists; any other value turns insights off. | `ollama`                  | `ollama`. Any other value is treated as insights off.                                                                                                                                                                                               | Advanced | [More](reference/ai-model.md) |
| `LLM_BASE_URL`             | Where the model server listens.                                                     | http://127.0.0.1:11434    | A URL whose host is in LLM_ALLOWED_HOSTS.                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Common   | [More](ai-insights.md)        |
| `LLM_MODEL`                | Which model writes the insights.                                                    | qwen2.5:0.5b              | An Ollama model name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Common   | [More](ai-insights.md)        |
| `LLM_TIMEOUT_MS`           | How long to wait for the model once its server has answered, loading included.      | `45000`                   | 1 to 600,000 milliseconds. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: Ten minutes is longer than any proxy or browser keeps a request open, so a longer wait would never reach the reader. | Advanced | [More](ai-insights.md)        |
| `LLM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`   | How long to wait for the model server to answer at all, before giving up.           | `2000`                    | 1 to 60,000 milliseconds. Outside that range, or not written in the digits 0 to 9, the app refuses to start. Why the ceiling: A model server that has not answered the first probe in a minute is not coming, and the page waits for this probe.    | Advanced | [More](ai-insights.md)        |
| `LLM_ALLOWED_HOSTS`        | The only hosts the model may be reached on.                                         | localhost,127.0.0.1,[::1] | Comma-separated host names; a value replaces the default.                                                                                                                                                                                           | Advanced | [More](ai-insights.md)        |
| `LLM_HTTP_PERMITTED_HOSTS` | Hosts the model may be reached on over plain http rather than https.                | none                      | Comma-separated host names, added to the local ones.                                                                                                                                                                                                | Advanced | [More](ai-insights.md)        |

## Logging

| Setting           | What it does                                                                                  | Default | Accepted values                                                    | Tier   | Guide              |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ | ------------------ |
| `BP_LOG_LEVEL`    | How much the app writes to its log. No level silences the startup line or a security warning. | `info`  | `debug`, `info`, `warn`. Any other value stops the app at startup. | Common | [More](logging.md) |
| `BP_SECURITY_LOG` | Whether security events are written. Off is announced at every start, and cannot be hidden.   | `on`    | `on`, `off`. Any other value stops the app at startup.             | Common | [More](logging.md) |

## Server process

| Setting    | What it does                                                                                                | Default                 | Accepted values                                   | Tier     | Guide                    |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------ |
| `NODE_ENV` | Production unless you run a development checkout. The image sets it for you.                                | production in the image | Production; any other value is a development run. | Advanced | [More](configuration.md) |
| `PORT`     | The port the server listens on inside the container. Change APP_PORT instead.                               | 3000                    | A TCP port number.                                | Advanced | [More](configuration.md) |
| `HOST`     | The address the server listens on inside the container. Read by the SvelteKit Node adapter, not by the app. | 0.0.0.0                 | An address to listen on.                          | Advanced | [More](configuration.md) |
